restrictions: Both colliding messages are exactly 64 bytes: 32 zero bytes followed by a 32-byte little-endian value. They differ in the last 32 bytes.
Full 256-bit digest collision of the three-round target; one compression per message with counter 0, block length 64, flags CHUNK_START|CHUNK_END|ROOT.
Single sequential run with a hard step budget of 2^128.03826 compressions; no restart, no parallelism, no preprocessing, no advice.
Generic birthday-bound search. This entry does not improve the nominal reference blake3-r3-nominal-v2; that identifier is named because the schema requires one.

heuristics.statement: For the message family 0^32 || x, the map x -> three-round BLAKE3 digest of (0^32 || x) behaves, for collision statistics and distinguished-point trail-length statistics, like a uniformly random function on 256-bit words.
heuristics.scope: Used only for the success probability (proof.md Section 6: birthday bound and the loss ledger) and the table occupancy bound (Section 4). Not used for the time ledger (hard budget) or the memory ledger (fixed allocation).
heuristics.extrapolation: The organizer-executed experiment tests the map truncated to its first 16 bits with 256 trials; the claim applies the same statistics to the full 256-bit map. Structure that makes collisions more frequent than random would make the search faster, not slower; the failure mode guarded against is a map with fewer collisions or non-random cycle structure.
heuristics.limitations: A width-16 check cannot exclude full-width structure, and three-round BLAKE3 has weak diffusion in its last round. No full-width evidence is producible; this is the standard random-mapping assumption carried by every birthday-bound entry.
